advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Normalize link_id to str (or None) at the record boundary so the stored value matches the `str | None` annotation regardless of backend id type.
evidence: apply_handlers.py:226-234: `store.record(str(local_id), str(target_local_id), str(relation), link_id=link_id, ...)` — link_id NOT str-wrapped though the other keys are
dispatch_apply_phases.py:413: `link_id = result.get("id") if isinstance(result, dict) else None` — no coercion of the id's type
advisory.finding: record()'s link_id parameter is typed `str | None`, but the value is passed straight through from `result.get("id")` (in _confirm_link_add) via _confirm to record() without str-normalization, while source_id/target_id/relation ARE wrapped with str() in the same callback. A backend that returns a non-string link id (e.g. an integer) is stored raw, contradicting the annotation.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _confirm (apply_handlers._make_link_confirm) or in record(), coerce: `link_id=str(link_id) if link_id is not None else None`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Short-circuit _make_link_confirm to return None when the mutation has no link ADD entries, avoiding an unnecessary store open for scalar-only updates.
evidence: apply_handlers.py:205-207: `local_id = mutation.get("local_id") ... if binding_store is None or not local_id: return None` — no check for the presence of link ADD entries
apply_handlers.py:215: `store = open_store(ctx.repo_root)` runs for every update with a binding_store
peer_confirmations.py:_load reads the JSON file on construction
advisory.finding: handle_update calls _make_link_confirm for every UPDATE mutation, and _make_link_confirm opens the store (open_store → disk read) whenever binding_store and local_id are present — regardless of whether the mutation has any link ADDs. Mutations that only touch scalar fields/comments still incur a per-mutation store load.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an early return when `not any(isinstance(e, dict) and e.get("action") == "add" for e in (mutation.get("links") or []))` before opening the store.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting peer_confirmations.STORE_RELATIVE equals git_adapter.PEER_CONFIRMATIONS_FILE (normalized), pinning the two path constants the docstring claims are pinned.
evidence: peer_confirmations.py: 'STORE_RELATIVE = os.path.join(".bridge_state", "peer_confirmations.json")' with comment 'Single-sourced against ``git_adapter.PEER_CONFIRMATIONS_FILE`` ... the two are pinned together by test.'
search of tests/unit/rebar_reconciler for STORE_RELATIVE returned (no matches); the promised pinning test does not exist
advisory.finding: The two independently-declared path constants that MUST agree — peer_confirmations.STORE_RELATIVE (.bridge_state/peer_confirmations.json) and git_adapter.PEER_CONFIRMATIONS_FILE — are never asserted equal, despite the module docstring stating 'Single-sourced against git_adapter.PEER_CONFIRMATIONS_FILE ... the two are pinned together by test.' If either drifts, the store writes/reads one filename while commit-back stages another, silently dropping all evidence, and no test would catch it.
scenarios: A maintainer renames git_adapter.PEER_CONFIRMATIONS_FILE (or changes BRIDGE_STATE_DIR) without updating STORE_RELATIVE: store writes a file commit-back never stages, or commit-back stages a file the store never writes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add: `assert peer_confirmations.STORE_RELATIVE == os.path.normpath(git_adapter.PEER_CONFIRMATIONS_FILE)` (or equivalent) in a dedicated test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that forces save() to hit its OSError branch (e.g. monkeypatch os.replace or open to raise OSError) and asserts save() returns without raising.
evidence: save() body: 'except OSError as exc: logger.warning("peer_confirmations: could not persist %s (%r)", self.path, exc); return' — this branch has no test
advisory.finding: PeerConfirmationStore.save()'s OSError fail-open branch (persist failure caught, logged, dirty flag left set) is never exercised. The suite's docstring asserts the store is 'strictly FAIL-OPEN' and calls the fail-open cases 'load-bearing', but only the READ path (corrupt/absent load) is tested; a write-path persist failure that should degrade silently has no regression coverage.
scenarios: Read-only tracker dir or os.replace failure during save(): the code must swallow and not raise; a future refactor that lets save() raise would break a landed outbound write, and no test guards this.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the extra 'first_confirmed_at' field in peer_confirmations.record() is intended, or drop it to match the ticket's enumerated record fields.
evidence: Ticket 248f scope: 'Record fields: link_id, direction (outbound | snapshot), confirmed_pass, confirmed_at (epoch ns), source (push | snapshot | backfill).' — first_confirmed_at is not listed.
advisory.finding: peer_confirmations.record() persists a 'first_confirmed_at' field that is not among the record fields the ticket enumerates (link_id, direction, confirmed_pass, confirmed_at, source, plus the source_id/target_id/relation key triple).
scenarios: Any record() write persists an unspecified provenance timestamp to the sidecar schema.
